findings.issue_text: [Critical/security] app/models/post.rb:131 — `cook` returns `raw` unmodified for `raw_html` posts and imported RSS content is stored unsanitized, allowing stored XSS via scripts/iframes in feeds; raw HTML must be sanitized before persistence or rendering
[Medium/security] app/models/topic_embed.rb:17 — raw URL is interpolated into single-quoted HTML attributes without escaping, allowing attribute breakout and injected markup/XSS in imported posts

[Medium/security] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` allows suffix matches (e.g. eviltrout.com.evil.com); should compare `e.origin === discourseUrl` after normalizing trailing slash
[Medium/security] app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:10 — `request.referer` is interpolated into an inline JS string with no escaping, allowing arbitrary JS injection; JSON-encode or strip quotes
[Medium/bug] app/views/embed/best.html.erb:7 — `<%- end if %>` compiles to a Ruby syntax error (`end if` with no condition), raising ActionView::SyntaxError; should be `<%- end -%>`

[Medium/concurrency] app/models/topic_embed.rb:23 — concurrent imports of the same URL both pass the `embed.blank?` check; the loser hits the unique index on `embed_url` and raises RecordNotUnique; handle/rescue or serialize per URL
[Medium/bug] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no `content`; a single missing-content item kills the whole polling run

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:21 — exact-host referer comparison blocks legit embedding on www. vs bare host mismatch, and referer may be absent for privacy-set browsers even for legitimate embeds

[Medium/data] app/models/topic_embed.rb:36-40 — `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` runs even if the revision didn't actually change/save the post, so stored sha1 no longer reflects content and future updates are skipped

[Low/performance] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no open/read timeout or size limit; a slow or huge feed blocks the scheduled job thread and retries pile up
[Low/bug] app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:7 — page reloads every 30 seconds forever with no error state when retrieval fails (network error, invalid feed, user not configured)
[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5 — if the page has no `#discourse-comments` element, `comments.appendChild(iframe)` throws a TypeError; should bail early when `comments` is null

[Low/test_gap] spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb — no test covers the 1-minute cache expiry combined with `current_user`, risking leaking personalized topic content to anonymous/proxied caches; also no tests for `absolutize_urls` port handling or non-HTTP schemes
[Low/doc_defect] lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 — the `category` (`-c`) option was silently removed from `disqus:import`; existing scripts will fail with unknown-option error and no changelog note exists

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

Candidate recommends strict equality after normalization, aligning with the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Critical/security] app/models/post.rb:131 — `cook` returns `raw` unmodified for `raw_html` posts and imported RSS content is stored unsanitized, allowing stored XSS via scripts/iframes in feeds; raw HTML must be sanitized before persistence or rendering

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook path where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). New RSS/remote imports explicitly set `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in `TopicEmbed.import` via `PostCreator` and pass `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` with `skip_validations: true`, but there is no sanitization of `contents` from feeds (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then imports it). The embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any script/iframe/etc in feed content would be stored and rendered, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] app/models/topic_embed.rb:17 — raw URL is interpolated into single-quoted HTML attributes without escaping, allowing attribute breakout and injected markup/XSS in imported posts

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends an HTML snippet containing `"#{url}"` into `contents` without escaping (`app/models/topic_embed.rb` around the `imported_from` line). The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows URLs containing single quotes or other characters that can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute and inject markup/attributes. This is especially dangerous because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly, bypassing the rendering/sanitization pipeline, and the embed view renders with `raw post.cooked`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] app/models/topic_embed.rb:23 — concurrent imports of the same URL both pass the `embed.blank?` check; the loser hits the unique index on `embed_url` and raises RecordNotUnique; handle/rescue or serialize per URL

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic check-then-insert: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so two concurrent imports of the same URL can both see `embed.blank?` and then one will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` on `create!`. The diff contains no rescue/handling, and the loser may also have already created a topic/post before failing, leaving inconsistent state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no `content`; a single missing-content item kills the whole polling run
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that calling `i.content.scrub` (via `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) will crash when a feed item lacks a `content` field (i.e., `i.content` is nil), causing a NoMethodError/nil pointer exception. The golden adds the idea of falling back to `description`, but the underlying bug is the same missing-content nil crash.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:21 — exact-host referer comparison blocks legit embedding on www. vs bare host mismatch, and referer may be absent for privacy-set browsers even for legitimate embeds

adjudication.rationale: The new `ensure_embeddable` check requires `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), which is an exact host match. This will reject legitimate embeds when the page is served from a common variant like `www.example.com` while the setting is `example.com`, and it also rejects cases where browsers omit the `Referer` header (the code turns nil into `''`, yielding `host == nil` and raising). This behavior is directly enforced by the diff and is likely to break embedding in real-world scenarios.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] app/models/topic_embed.rb:36-40 — `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` runs even if the revision didn't actually change/save the post, so stored sha1 no longer reflects content and future updates are skipped

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed is updated, the code does:

```rb
revisor.revise!(...)
embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)
```

inside the `if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` block. The result of `revise!` is not checked, and nothing guards against `revise!` returning `false` (e.g., `PostRevisor#revise!` explicitly returns `false` when `should_revise?` is false). In that case, `content_sha1` will still be updated even though the post content wasn’t changed/saved, so the stored SHA1 can diverge from what’s actually in the post and later imports with the same SHA1 will be skipped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no open/read timeout or size limit; a slow or huge feed blocks the scheduled job thread and retries pile up

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the feed is fetched via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` or size limiting, so a slow/large feed can block the Sidekiq worker thread running the scheduled job. However, the finding’s claim that “retries pile up” isn’t supported here because the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:7 — page reloads every 30 seconds forever with no error state when retrieval fails (network error, invalid feed, user not configured)

adjudication.rationale: The new loading template unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` after 30 seconds (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), and `EmbedController#best` renders this template whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil. If the background retrieval never succeeds (e.g., network/open-uri failure in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, invalid feed in `Jobs::PollFeed`, or missing `embed_by_username` user causing `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` to return), there is no error/timeout state in the controller or view, so the iframe will keep reloading forever.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5 — if the page has no `#discourse-comments` element, `comments.appendChild(iframe)` throws a TypeError; should bail early when `comments` is null

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `comments` is assigned via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then used unconditionally in `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the element is absent, `comments` will be `null` and this will throw a `TypeError` at runtime. The diff contains no guard/bail-out for this case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb — no test covers the 1-minute cache expiry combined with `current_user`, risking leaking personalized topic content to anonymous/proxied caches; also no tests for `absolutize_urls` port handling or non-HTTP schemes

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbedController#best`, which builds `@topic_view = TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` and sets `discourse_expires_in 1.minute`, but the new controller spec doesn’t assert anything about cache headers/variation with `current_user`, so the review comment about a missing test for caching behavior is diff-grounded. Separately, `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` contains explicit port logic (`prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`) that isn’t covered by the added specs, so the “port handling” test gap is also grounded. However, the mention of “non-HTTP schemes” is less applicable because `TopicEmbed.import` returns early unless the URL matches `^https?://`, so that part overreaches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 — the `category` (`-c`) option was silently removed from `disqus:import`; existing scripts will fail with unknown-option error and no changelog note exists

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the related `category_id` lookup/usage, replacing topic creation with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)`. This is a real, diff-grounded backward-incompatible CLI change: any existing `disqus:import` invocations passing `-c/--category` will now raise an unknown option error in Thor. The claim about “no changelog note exists” cannot be verified from this diff, but the silent option removal itself is verifiable.
